Harness

The execution layer around a model

components.name: Definition comparison
components.description: Neutral source-labeled views precede scope and boundaries. Context, attribution and editorial interpretation stay visible without adoption color.
components.html:
ASD advisory

Institutional; security and governance

ASD uses harness for the non-LLM components of an agentic system, including connections to tools, data, memory and planning workflows, privileges and the control loop. [4]

SWE-agent architecture

Peer-reviewed; agent-computer interface

SWE-agent supplies a task-oriented interface for a language-model agent to navigate repositories, edit files and execute tests. This informs the runtime boundary; the paper is not treated as a general definition of Harness. [15] Editorial interpretation

Managed Agents architecture

First-party; product boundary

Anthropic separates session, harness and sandbox. Its harness drives the loop and routes model-requested tool calls; the sandbox executes them. [5]

Conceptual proposal

Preprint; not established consensus

Macedo proposes an operational boundary against SDKs, frameworks, IDE plugins, evaluation scaffolds and orchestrators. This is one author’s definition proposal. [6]

narrative.overview:
The approved fusion combines B's persistent searchable navigation with A's editorial reading layout. Warm paper, green ink and generous paragraph rhythm support finding a meaning quickly, then reading its scope, boundaries and sources carefully. This records the built static glossary rather than the comparison prototype's routing or provisional details.

Navigation uses Manrope, a stable index and an explicit current term. Newsreader gives titles, term rows and definitions a publication character. Neutral comparison rows make competing definitions and their evidence visible; compact semantic tags distinguish the Repository proposal from documented adoption. Light and dark appearances share the same hierarchy; no animation or authored transition is applied.
keyCharacteristics: Persistent searchable index paired with a flexible reading column.
Warm neutral surfaces, dark green ink and restrained green links.
Newsreader for reading landmarks; Manrope for navigation and ordinary prose.
Flat surfaces with tonal selection and thin structural dividers.
Static term addresses and native HTML enhanced by local search.

rules.name: The Semantic Appearance Rule
rules.body: Switch all six roles together. Honor the system color preference until the reader chooses Light or Dark; store that choice per tab and site base path.

rules.name: The Adoption Evidence Rule
rules.body: Reserve yellow and green status fills for internal adoption. Green requires a documented consensus decision; external source rank never inherits adoption color. Switch the status ink/paper pairs with the appearance.

rules.name: The Two Reading Speeds Rule
rules.body: Use the serif for term names and core meanings; use the sans-serif for retrieval, comparison labels, section labels, ordinary prose and evidence records.

rules.name: The Reading Space Rule
rules.body: Move supporting records after the article before compressing the text into a narrow three-column layout.

rules.name: The Flat Reference Rule
rules.body: Use structural rules and tonal states to distinguish regions; retain the calm, flat reading surface.

rules.name: The Strict Nesting Rule
rules.body: Nest only a documented is-a relationship. Keep composition and control relationships visibly typed, with their conditions and evidence beside them.

rules.name: Peripheral Legibility
rules.body: Use 14px header and page-directory text, 15px catalog terms and at least 13px auxiliary labels; keep the larger serif reading hierarchy.

rules.name: Canonical Comparison
rules.body: Maintain one cited comparison section, link to its anchor from related terms, and stack table cells with visible labels on phones.

dos: **Do** preserve the approved persistent navigation and editorial reading pairing.
**Do** use all six semantic color roles together in light and dark appearance.
**Do** keep search visible on mobile and related links outside search filtering.
**Do** preserve native anchors, catalog disclosure, keyboard focus and static fallbacks.
**Do** retain glossary prose, versioned sources and the distinction between proposal and adoption.
**Do** keep comparison views, source tiers and editorial interpretations neutral, reserving adoption fills for explicit internal status.
**Do** use strict subtype nesting only for is-a and retain cited conditions for uses and supports/orchestrates.
donts: **Don't** replace the self-hosted reading fonts with a system display face.
**Don't** convert open definition rows into lifted cards or add decorative shadows.
**Don't** compress the desktop marginal column into the mobile article.
**Don't** put the query in URLs or send search input to a server.
**Don't** introduce decorative eyebrows above the homepage, term title or build-record title.
**Don't** show green adoption status without a recorded consensus decision.
